text: Good API design makes applications easier to build and maintain. When creating REST APIs, you should use clear and consistent endpoints, such as `/users/123` instead of confusing paths. Always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation helps other developers understand how your API works, so they can use it without guessing. You should also plan for versioning, for example by adding `/v1/` to your URLs, so that future changes don't break existing users. Following these practices saves time and reduces mistakes for everyone.
